title: Analyzing Income Statements
overview: Income-statement analysis separates sustainable operating performance from accounting choices and unusual items.
example: Follow one transaction through the income statement, balance sheet, cash-flow statement, and the resulting ratios.

modules.title: Revenue Recognition
modules.explanation: Income-statement analysis asks when revenue and expenses are recognized and whether reported profit is sustainable. Classification, estimates, unusual items, dilution, and common-size margins can materially change comparisons.
steps: Identify the economic event and the recognition rule applied to it.
Separate recurring operations from financing, tax, and unusual effects.
Normalize where justified and explain the effect on margins and per-share results.
modules.check: Explain how revenue recognition changes an analyst's conclusion, including one limitation.
objectives: Explain revenue recognition in plain language and connect it to the reading's central problem.
Apply the analytical decision rule or analytical decision rule with clearly labeled inputs.
Interpret the result, challenge its assumptions, and identify one condition that would change the conclusion.
lesson: Income-statement analysis asks when revenue and expenses are recognized and whether reported profit is sustainable. Classification, estimates, unusual items, dilution, and common-size margins can materially change comparisons.

Statement analysis follows an economic event through recognition, measurement, presentation, disclosure, and cash flow. Comparability often requires adjustments because firms can represent similar economics with different estimates or classifications.

For revenue recognition, begin by asking what decision is being made and what evidence is available. Then follow the three-step method below. The final answer should state both the conclusion and the most important reason it may fail.

keyTerms.definition: Income-statement analysis asks when revenue and expenses are recognized and whether reported profit is sustainable. Classification, estimates, unusual items, dilution, and common-size margins can materially change comparisons.
The decision to record an item in the primary financial statements.
The amount and basis used to report a recognized item.
The degree to which reported earnings reflect sustainable performance and convert into cash.

formula.label: Analytical decision rule
formula.interpretation: A defensible conclusion makes the evidence and assumptions visible, follows a repeatable process, and states what could change the decision.
formula.example: For revenue recognition, an analyst applies the stated process, compares the result with an alternative, and records the most important limitation.

formula.label: Basic EPS
formula.expression: EPS = (net income − preferred dividends) / weighted-average common shares
formula.interpretation: Use the shares outstanding during the period rather than only the closing balance.
formula.example: Income available to common of 12 million over 6 million weighted shares gives EPS of 2.
